evidence_summary: Two dictionary editions give BUCAS as tomorrow while the modern orthography explains that native Kapampangan uses K rather than inherited Spanish C or Q.
conflict_or_risk: This supports the specific pair but not an unrestricted global C-to-K rewrite.

claim: Kapampangan root meaning come or arrive
evidence_summary: Independent dictionary and teaching sources give datang as a verb meaning come or arrive.
conflict_or_risk: No new segmentation boundary is justified because datang is the root itself.

claim: Attested in one proposed Kapampangan example sentence
evidence_summary: The exact sentence Bukas na datang ing pangulo appears in the Kapampangan side of a comparative paper.
conflict_or_risk: The source conflicts with stronger instructional evidence and does not establish a morpheme boundary.

claim: Filipino equivalent rather than the listed Kapampangan headword
evidence_summary: The Kapampangan entries are pamuntuk and presidenti while pangulo occurs in the Filipino column.
conflict_or_risk: The trilingual list is unattributed and should support but not solely decide adjudication.

claim: Kapampangan instructional and orthographic form for president
evidence_summary: Grammar teaching and orthography sources use presidente or accented presidénti for president.
conflict_or_risk: Changing source text would be normalization or translation editing rather than morphological segmentation.

claim: Kapampangan lexical item used for a head or leader and glossed chairman or president
evidence_summary: The trilingual list gives pamuntuk as chairman or president and the orthography history uses Pamuntuk contextually for a former head.
conflict_or_risk: Its exact equivalence to a national president in every register remains a translation choice.

conflict_or_risk: The one-vowel difference from pangulo is semantically material and is not evidence for a spelling rewrite.

claim: Standalone syntactic enclitic with multiple homophonous functions
evidence_summary: Richards describes time-particle na and pa as enclitics and distinguishes time na from request na and third-person singular agentive na.
conflict_or_risk: The current per-pretoken diagnostic labels standalone na as a protected root and cannot contextually disambiguate these homophones.

claim: Morphophonemic fusion of two clitic or agreement forms
evidence_summary: Richards explicitly lists na plus ya yielding ne alongside ku plus ya yielding ke and mu plus ya yielding me.
conflict_or_risk: The paper inventory treats ne as an atomic clitic and changing that contract would require method reconciliation and retraining.

claim: Documented co-occurring formative prefix and suffix patterns
evidence_summary: Richards describes pag- or paN- with -an occurring around a verb root.
conflict_or_risk: The thesis implementation intentionally permits only its paper-declared affix inventory so this cannot be added silently.
